title: Getting started with Bun
author: Ana Souza
body: Bun is a JavaScript runtime, package manager and test runner in one binary. In this post we install it, create a project with bun init and run our first script.

title: Why we moved our API to Hono
author: Marcus Lee
body: Our old Express app needed a dozen middlewares before it could answer a request. Hono gave us routing, validation and typed handlers with a much smaller footprint, and it runs on every platform we deploy to.

title: Validating requests with Zod
author: Priya Nair
body: A schema is the contract between your API and its clients. With Zod you write it once and get both runtime validation and static types, so a bad payload never reaches your handler.

title: A gentle introduction to edge functions
author: Ana Souza
body: Edge functions run close to your users, start in milliseconds and scale to zero. They suit small APIs, redirects and personalization, and they are a poor fit for long-running jobs.

title: Five things I wish I knew about SQLite
author: Tom Becker
body: Turn on WAL mode, use prepared statements, index the columns you filter on, keep transactions short and back up with the online backup API. SQLite will take you much further than you think.

title: Writing tests that do not lie
author: Priya Nair
body: A test that mocks everything proves only that the mocks work. Test behavior through public interfaces, keep fixtures small and make every failure message tell you what broke.

title: Caching HTTP responses the right way
author: Marcus Lee
body: Cache-Control, ETag and Vary decide who may store a response and for how long. Get them right and your CDN does most of the work; get them wrong and users see each other's pages.

title: Deploying a TypeScript API in five minutes
author: Ana Souza
body: Export your app's fetch handler, push to the main branch and let the platform build it. We walk through environment variables, logs and rolling back a bad deploy.

title: What is a JWT, really?
author: Tom Becker
body: A JSON Web Token is a signed JSON object, not an encrypted one. Anyone can read its claims, so keep secrets out of it and always verify the signature and the expiry on the server.

title: Notes from our first production incident
author: Priya Nair
body: At 3 a.m. a migration locked the orders table for eleven minutes. Here is the timeline, what our alerts missed and the three changes we made to our deploy checklist.

title: Server-side rendering without a framework
author: Marcus Lee
body: renderToString turns a React tree into HTML in a single call. Pair it with a fetch handler and you have a server-rendered page in about thirty lines of code.

title: Keeping dependencies up to date
author: Tom Becker
body: Pin exact versions, update on a schedule and read the changelog before you merge. A lockfile makes builds repeatable, but it does not make old packages safe.
